title: How Coinbase scaled AI to 1,000+ engineers | Chintan Turakhia
summary: Coinbase engineering director describes driving AI adoption across a large org through hands-on leadership, PR speedruns, shared wins and an internal ticket-to-PR agent.

assertions.quote: the worst thing any leader could do is just be like, I decree you must use AI.

verdicts.note: Reports of token-maxing and resentment support it, but some mandated rollouts (e.g. Shopify, Coinbase) report adoption gains; evidence is anecdotal either way.

assertions.quote: People opened it up, checked the box, did kind of like a hello world thing, but it didn't stick

verdicts.note: Adoption and gains vary widely across teams and DORA finds organizational practices matter, but evidence isolating training effects is mostly observational.

assertions.quote: we chipped away and we put in a bunch of rules like cursor rules and that that helps so much.

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.

assertions.quote: I just did like you know 20 unit tests and then went and had a coffee.

verdicts.note: AI speeds drafting tests and docs, but generated tests often assert implementation details or weak properties and need review.

assertions.quote: we built this internal bot. I'm excited to show you. And within seconds like the PR is being authored, right? an agent picks it up

verdicts.note: Background agents do produce usable PRs for well-scoped chores, but merge rates vary widely and many PRs need iteration; 'most of the time' is optimistic.

assertions.quote: context is the most important thing. So the place where we capture all of our context is linear

verdicts.note: Relevant org context plausibly cuts rework, but the cited 50% token / one-shot result is a single vendor test, not independent evidence.

assertions.quote: lines of code committed by AI. I think that's like kind of misleading

verdicts.note: Accepted suggestions are often later rewritten or deleted, and output volume has long been a poor proxy for productivity; controlled studies measure task time or delivery instead.

assertions.quote: does that count as a replacement for people and like I'm in the camp of absolutely not. AI is an accelerant

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.
